From: Jen Park <jen.park@summitly.ai>

Cc: Alex Gomez <alexg@summitly.ai>
Date: Sat, 14 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Summitly x Redwood - LangChain adapter commercial pilot (SOW attached)

Hi Nikhil,

Great to meet last week — excited to keep momentum. Summitly has a lightweight LangChain adapter and prompt-optimization tooling that several ISVs have adopted; BrightFund (our mutual contact) is keen to run a short commercial pilot to validate cost/latency and end-to-end tracing into their observability stack.

Attached is a draft SOW that outlines a 6-week pilot (integration + joint evaluation) and our completed security questionnaire. High-level asks from Summitly:
- Redwood to host the adapter behind a dedicated route for BrightFund (pilot capacity ~10k requests/day)
- Trace integration so BrightFund can see call-level tracing in their Datadog instance
- Joint performance benchmarks (latency P50/P95, tokens/sec)

Would Redwood be open to a co-signed pilot SOW and a kickoff week of Mar 1? We can provide a small pilot PO (covers engineering time + shared infra).

Attachments: Summitly_Redwood_SOW_v1.pdf, summitly_security_questionnaire_filled.xlsx

Thanks — Jen

--
Jen Park
Head of Partnerships | Summitly
jen.park@summitly.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 14 Feb 2027 11:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Summitly x Redwood - LangChain adapter commercial pilot (SOW attached)

Jen — thanks for the materials and the clear scope.

We'd be happy to run a time-boxed commercial pilot with BrightFund. A few quick clarifying items before we sign:
- Throughput/SLA: the SOW references ~10k req/day. Can you confirm expected concurrency and typical seq length (avg tokens/input + generated tokens)? This affects capacity profile and whether we recommend a dedicated pool vs. reserved burst.
- Data residency: BrightFund needs EU data-at-rest for production. For the pilot is US-hosted acceptable, or do they require EU-hosted test infra?
- Tracing: are you expecting Redwood to emit traces to Summitly's Datadog account, or do you want Summitly to consume logs via Redwoods' console? We can do both with a short webhook/forwarder.

Mar 1 kickoff is feasible for our engineering calendar. I've looped in Karthik (runtime/instrumentation) and Marissa (partner integrations) to scope the onboarding tasks. Stephanie from PM will own rollout/milestone tracking.

If you can confirm concurrency + residency, we'll internally draft a short Redwood SOW addendum and route for signature. We can accept a PO for the pilot; please include the billing contact in the DocuSign envelope.

Best,
Nikhil

--
Nikhil Sharma
Director, Strategic Partnerships | Redwood Inference

Subject: Fwd: Summitly x Redwood - LangChain adapter commercial pilot (SOW attached)

Team — forwarding Summitly's SOW and questionnaire. We have a potential pilot with BrightFund; kickoff target Mar 1. High-level asks (from Jen): dedicated route for adapter, tracing integration to Summitly/Datadog, joint perf benchmarks. They will provide a PO to cover pilot costs.

Proposed internal owners and immediate tasks:
- Karthik: validate runtime changes needed for LangChain adapter (tracer hook points, per-call metadata, and preferred metric emitters). Can you estimate ~days of effort and confirm whether we need a short runtime release?
- Marissa: partner onboarding flow (sandbox credentials, route provisioning, SSO for Summitly engineers if needed), plus coordinate billing/PO contact.
- Stephanie: draft the Redwood SOW addendum (1 page) with acceptance criteria (latency bench, functional verification, trace visibility) and identify the DocuSign contact.

Other tech notes:
- We should avoid early EU infra commitments for the pilot unless BrightFund insists — keeps time-to-kickoff faster.
- Instrumentation: prefer emitting OpenTelemetry spans; Summitly indicated Datadog but they said they'd accept OTLP to a forwarder.

Please reply with ETA estimates so I can get back to Jen.

Thanks — Nikhil

- Residency: pilot is fine in US. EU will be contextual for production only.
- Tracing: Summitly prefers Redwood to forward OpenTelemetry spans to our Datadog account; we'll share account creds and Alex will handle the wiring.
